answer: An operator running many aliases therefore burns for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the cipher quota and the lagoon admission check. Submission rate is limited to 3 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole swarm from one uplink. Because the counters live in the timber ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
